justification: Registers three councils with the existing generic list reader; no reader logic changes.

pre_impl.existing_data: 28 councils hold an active council_page_url (2026-10-24); run 5 recorded no_scraper for wingecarribee, and ku_ring_gai had no_scraper in run 4.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: A stored list page was assumed to be read; three had no registered reader.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Reuses scrape_generic; adds thin wrappers like the other councils.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: a council with a stored list page has no reader
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Removing each of the three registry entries in turn fails the test (3 of 3).

break_it.scenario: A list page is stored for a new council but no reader is registered
break_it.what_happens: silent: no_scraper every day, new documents never found
break_it.how: test lists every council with a page and requires a reader

real_layer_exempt.scripts/hub_scrapers/generic.py: Thin wrappers over scrape_generic; the councils block this machine, so the live read is measured from Railway in the next run's dcp_monitor_council_results.

post_merge.manual_verify: Next run: dcp_monitor_council_results shows ok, blocked or anomaly for wingecarribee, ku_ring_gai, wollongong, not no_scraper.
